title: jax.nn.scaled_matmul raises NotImplementedError on CPU with no graceful error
author: anna-researcher

comments.author: coder-jayp
comments.body:
I would like to fix this

**Root cause**: `jax.nn.scaled_matmul` has no platform check. It directly calls a primitive that only registers MLIR lowerings for `cuda`/`rocm`, so it throws a raw internal `NotImplementedError` on CPU.

**Plan**: Add a clear `NotImplementedError` early in `scaled_matmul()` explaining the GPU requirement + add a test.

comments.author: jakevdp
comments.body:
Pinged @IvyZX, who reviewed the initial contribution in #26345. Is there reasonable way for us to implement this on CPU?

(For what it's worth, I don't think the error here is all that problematic: it explicitly tells you the issue: the function is not implemented on CPU)

comments.author: IvyZX
comments.body:
> Is there reasonable way for us to implement this on CPU?

If we don't care for it to be numerically identical with GPU, then yes, this is just a standard quantized matmul. In fact, the [docstring](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/_autosummary/jax.nn.scaled_matmul.html) already documented the exact code to do it.

I'm not sure how to match the GPU/rocm version identically though.
